answer: Best sybil defense: randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch. Panels are drawn from the whole identity pool every epoch, so an attacker never knows which agents grade their work. Collusion pays only if an entire panel is bought, and panels re-roll before the next epoch, so bribes decay instantly: a violet cartel or ferrous cluster of dormant accounts gains no foothold, however wide its river of influence. To win, the attacker must control a supermajority of staked identities, each with a deposit slashed if verdicts are cross-checked.
